title: How to use TEXTJOIN in Excel
description: Learn how Excel TEXTJOIN combines text across cells and ranges with a delimiter, with a worked example and a link to hands-on practice.

args.name: delimiter
args.text: The character or string to place between each text item, enclosed in double quotes (such as ", " or "-").

args.name: ignore_empty
args.text: Set to TRUE to skip empty cells, or FALSE to include them and retain extra delimiters.

args.name: text1
args.text: The first text item, cell reference, or range to merge.

args.name: text2
args.text: Additional text items, cell references, or ranges to include in the combined result.

sections.heading: What TEXTJOIN does
sections.text: **TEXTJOIN** merges text from multiple cells or ranges into a single string. You provide a delimiterâ€”such as a comma or spaceâ€”and Excel inserts it between each value. You can also tell it to skip empty cells automatically.

sections.heading: A small example
sections.text: Here is a list of workshop sessions and speakers. The formula in the blank result cell joins all speaker names into one comma-separated list.

sections.heading: Skip blank cells
sections.text: Set `ignore_empty` to `TRUE` to ignore blank cells in your range. If you set it to `FALSE`, Excel includes those empty cells, leaving repeated delimiters such as `Alex, , Elena`.

sections.heading: Common mistake: delimiter without quotes
sections.text: Always enclose text delimiters in quotation marks, such as `"-"`. Typing `=TEXTJOIN(-, TRUE, B2:B4)` won't be accepted: Excel shows a formula error message and the formula is never entered. Also keep the argument order in mind: delimiter first, then `ignore_empty`, then your text range.
